news.title: 3 embarrassing questions: FIFA amends its regulations after the 2026 World Cup crisis
news.lede: Trump's intervention sparked a great deal of controversy, and the international federation is paying the price. FIFA, the International Federation of Association Football, has decided to amend Article 27 of its Disciplinary Code after the storm whipped up by the case of American forward Folarin Balogun. Balogun played in a World Cup match despite being sent off in the previous one. The Belgian Football Association objected and demanded official clarification of how it had happened.

news.title: Powerchair Football World Cup 2026: England among the favourites
news.lede: Colin Gordon will be coaching Argentina at the World Cup, while son Chris will be playing for England. "I was a big football fan growing up. My dad got involved with powerchair football through me," England goalkeeper Chris Gordon says of his father Colin. "But he's now coaching Argentina, so we'll be facing each other in the World Cup."

news.title: Gianni Infantino issues public apology as FIFA announces massive $6.35 billion investment plan following World Cup success
news.lede: Massive funding package unveiledFIFA President Infantino issued a public apology following the latest FIFA Council meeting at the Home of FIFA in Zurich. The chief executive addressed past mistakes regarding the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which has now been permanently withdrawn.Despite the governance setback, FIFA presented a landmark financial initiative called the FIFA Surplus Solidarity Programme. Driven by exceptional commercial returns from the 48-team 2026 World Cup, the plan will more than double development funding for the 2027-2030 period.The total support package will reach $6.35 billion, drawing from an estimated cycle surplus of between $5.2 billion and $5.6 billion. Infantino took responsibility for how the project was handled and communicated to the global football community."

news.title: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at FIFA meeting over World Cup plan
news.lede: Updated Oct. 16, 2026, 9:18 a.m. FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologised for mistakes surrounding a failed plan to bring private investors into the World Cup, but Council members say key questions remain unanswered. FIFA president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project. "We asked a great many critical questions, but there were no satisfactory answers from my point of view," said Bernd Neuendorf, the head of the German Football Association (DFB), who is also a member of the FIFA Council.

news.title: Challenging opponents await Young Football Ferns at U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: The second of five FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cups in Morocco gets underway this weekend, with New Zealand continuing a run of consecutive qualifications since its inception in 2008. FIFA has made the tournament an annual competition to allow more opportunities for players, with Morocco awarded hosting rights from 2025 until 2029. The tournament will be hosted predominantly at the Mohammed VI Football Academy in Salé, opposite the capital Rabat where the semifinals, third-place playoff and final will be held at the 22,000-capacity Moulay El Hassan Stadium. Some 24 teams will participate, with the top two in each group and the best four third-placed teams advancing to the knockout rounds.
